title: The synthetic set that memorized one entity
blurb: Totals hid entity collapse and timeouts were admitted.
prompt: A synthetic dataset passed review on total counts while containing ten thousand variants of one seed entity, and judge timeouts were admitted as fine. The model-generated draft throttles no entity and admits unscored records. Review it, fix it, and prove diversity is measured and scoring is complete.
aiNote: The draft enforces only a global record cap with no per-entity throttle, so a recipe can collapse onto one prolific seed without any metric noticing, and it admits judge-timeout records as likely fine, converting infra flakiness into silent label noise.
testIdea: Generate with a single dominant seed entity and assert per-entity limits throttle it; time out the judge and assert the record is parked and counted; trace a sampled admitted record back to its seed digest.
followUps: What diversity metric actually predicts utility?
How do license flags classify derivative synthetic data?
What review sample size makes a synthetic set shippable?
